title: Minimax Neyman Regret under Outcome-Dependent Reporting Delays at the Critical Tail Exponent
banked_reason: Math review passes, but the exact critical reporting value, certified computation, and attaining policy remain open; achieved incremental below the required field floor. Independent validity gate confirms no bounded same-topic repair.
gap_reasons: The field-level promised object—an exact convergent value or evaluated envelopes, an attaining policy, and a certified value algorithm—is still posed as an open question; the current derivation supplies only a lower certificate and a coarse feasible upper bound, so it does not yet deliver the headline kernel.
For informative reporting, they establish only the bracket between 9/8+(25/32)β*L² and 217(1+L²), leaving the coefficient far from determined.
Open-ended Question critical-value retains limit existence, an evaluable exact value or nonconvergent envelopes, and an attaining policy—the central advertised research object.
The finite prefix saddle certificates concern easier diagnostic experiments and do not establish equivalence to stochastic reporting with unknown lag masses.
proof_attempt_summary: Derived the exact immediate-feedback regret constant 9/8 and a strictly positive informative-reporting logarithmic penalty, alongside a legal coarse upper bound. The exact full-reporting value or evaluated envelopes, certified algorithm and attaining policy remain open; diagnostic prefix games do not establish the required two-way chronological transfer. D0.5 math passed, but the achieved tier is incremental below the field floor; independent validity review confirmed no bounded repair, and formalization was not launched.
tldr: Informative reporting can conceal the arm second moments that determine precision-optimal treatment allocation even when final followup is complete. The focal object is the exact all-policy logarithmic minimax cost \(G_L(T)/\log T\) at reporting-tail exponent \(1/2\), conditional on the bespoke model restriction \(m\in[1/4,1]^2\), with an independently derived immediate-feedback benchmark on the same moment box. The fixed floor describes common-outcome populations on a prespecified bounded measurement scale; it is not a standard condition supported by the direct-feedback literature. The research question requires an evaluable limiting value, an attaining chronological policy, and a matching lower bound on the same observable experiment, or explicitly evaluated nonconvergent envelopes. Posterior Jensen gaps and legal multiscale hidden bands provide the starting reductions; the reporting-aware information transfer and certified computation remain central proof obligations.
gap: Published immediate-feedback Neyman-regret bounds and conditionally noninformative delayed-design results do not give the exact all-policy cumulative raw-HT coefficient under arbitrary outcome-selected reporting. Their results do not supply the bespoke fixed lower raw-moment floor imposed here.
fill: The target is a chronological information reduction on \(\mathcal M_L\) with both design recovery and a same-information converse, followed by certified evaluation of the exact extra reporting cost relative to \(\mathcal M_0\). Both classes retain the bespoke floor. A coarse logarithmic rate alone does not fill this gap.
